learning_outcomes.text: Students know the essential methods and procedures for the technical design of machine elements: static determinacy, force and moment flow, stress-appropriate design, assembly and disassembly-appropriate design, as well as material and manufacturing-appropriate design.
Students know the design of castings, welded joints, axles and shafts, and bearings.
Students are able to distinguish between types of stress.
Students are able to compare stress and load capacity and determine a safety factor.
Students are able to perform standard-compliant calculations for machine elements.
Students know the FKM guideline "Analytical strength verification for machine components".
Students are familiar with the design of shafts, shaft-hub connections, and rolling bearings.
Students know the basics of lubricant selection.
Students know engineering science fundamentals in the field of strength theory and machine elements.
Students can understand, explain and apply technical standard calculations.
Students can transfer knowledge/skills to specific mechanical engineering / engineering science problems.

syllabus_topics: Strength theory applied to shaft-hub connections
Strength theory applied to rolling bearings
Application of calculation regulations according to respective standards
Creation of technical design calculations for machine elements
Creation of technical documentation for these calculations
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written exam. The grade's contribution to the final grade is determined by the Bachelor's examination regulations.
